9.  Proposed Short- Term Rental  Community Development Director Scherer reported on the proposed Short-
  Ordinance  Term Rental Ordinance.  He stated that at the Council' s May 3, 2021, meeting,

  a public hearing was conducted and concluded. The Ordinance required minor
  technical changes and is being brought back to the Council at this meeting
  with the recommendation to waive further reading, and to introduce Ordinance
  No. 1098, and place on first reading. The Ordinance will take effect on August
  17, 2021,  when the current moratorium  expires.

  Mayor called for public comment on this matter.

  There was none.

  It was moved by Carder, seconded by Lau, and unanimously carried by roll call
  to waive further reading and place on first reading Ordinance No. 1098,

  Councii Member Carder reported on a Free Etching on Catalytic Converters
  Event hosted by the La Verne Police Department in collaboration with Sanders
  Towing. She thanked the La Verne Police Department staff and Sanders
  Towing. She also thanked Hollie Savage of the La Verne Police for organizing
  the event.  She stated it was  a great  community  event.  She congratulated the
  Bonita High School Girls' Varsity Soccer Team for placing second in the play-
  offs. She stated that the City is safe, and that public safety is the City' s
  number  one  concern.  She stated that the City Council supports all the City
  departments.  She stated that Station No. 3 would be reopened once the City
  hires Firefighter  Paramedics.

  Council Member Lau spoke about the importance vaccinations and for
  residents  to do their part  and  get vaccinated.  She urged everyone to be kind,
  stay  safe  and  wear your  mask.  She thanked the residents for their
  participation  in tonight' s meeting.

  Mayor Pro Davis stated that we were not finished with COVID- 19 yet, but there
  was good news about reopening, but the City would still have to wait for the
  State  and  County for COVID- 19 guidelines.  He spoke about participating in an
  event recognizing  school  certified  employees.  He spoke about the Los
  Angeles County Fair holding a light fair event.  He stated that with the merger
  of Leroy' s Haynes and David Margaret Homes it should help with the problems
  at  David and Margaret.  He stated that City Staff discussion is important and
  that all City Departments are important.
  Mayor Hepburn thanked the Public Works staff for their presentation and great
  job on SB 1383.  He thanked Senior Management Analyst Lopez for her work
  on the financial report. He too, congratulated the Girls' Varsity Soccer team.
  He spoke  about  COVID- 19 vaccines.  He urged everyone to get vaccinated
  and  for those who have not to get their second  shots.  He stated that we

  would be all safer with more people vaccinated.
